record.paper_title: Open questions in quarkonium and electromagnetic probes
record.context_brief: Overall evidentiary status of new-physics claims
record.original_question: Do the experimental data available for quarkonium production and electromagnetic probes in high-energy heavy-ion collisions already provide convincing evidence, beyond reasonable doubt, for the existence of genuinely new physics in those collisions, rather than effects that can still be explained by uncertainties in baseline measurements and conventional nuclear processes?

evidence.quote: having in mind the most important of all the open questions: do we have, today, from experimental data on electromagnetic probes and quarkonium production, convincing evidence that shows, beyond reasonable doubt, the existence of "new physics" in high-energy heavy-ion collisions?

we do not yet have convincing evidence, from experimental data on quarkonium or electromagnetic probes, that shows beyond reasonable doubt the existence of "new physics" in high-energy heavy-ion collisions.

artifact.category_tag: quarkonium and electromagnetic probes in heavy-ion collisions
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the body of experimental measurements obtained in high-energy heavy-ion collisions concerning (i) quarkonium production yields (e.g., J/ψ, ψ(2S), Υ states and their suppression or enhancement patterns relative to proton–proton or proton–nucleus baselines), and (ii) electromagnetic probes (direct photons and dilepton invariant-mass spectra in the low, intermediate, and high mass regions). Let a "conventional baseline explanation" denote any combination of (a) measured or extrapolated proton–proton and proton–nucleus reference cross sections with their quoted uncertainties, (b) cold nuclear matter effects (nuclear parton distribution modifications, initial-state energy loss, nuclear absorption, Cronin-like broadening), and (c) standard hadronic-phase contributions (resonance decays, hadronic rescattering, in-medium hadron production) treated within accepted modeling uncertainties. Define "new physics in heavy-ion collisions" to mean phenomena that cannot be accommodated by any such conventional baseline explanation — in particular, signatures requiring deconfined partonic matter, chiral symmetry restoration, or thermal radiation from a quark-gluon plasma. 

Question: Do the currently available experimental data on quarkonium production and on electromagnetic probes in high-energy heavy-ion collisions, taken together, establish the existence of new physics in the above sense beyond reasonable doubt, in the precise sense that no conventional baseline explanation (within stated experimental and theoretical uncertainties of the references and cold/hot hadronic effects) is compatible with the observed yields, spectra, and centrality/system-size dependences?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether quarkonium suppression and electromagnetic-probe measurements definitively establish new physics (e.g., a deconfined quark-gluon plasma) beyond baseline and cold-nuclear-matter uncertainties is widely regarded as still open in the heavy-ion community. While LHC-era results (sequential Υ suppression, regeneration of charmonium, thermal photon and dilepton observations) have strengthened the QGP interpretation, recent reviews continue to emphasize baseline and CNM uncertainties as limiting factors and have not declared the matter settled beyond reasonable doubt.

status_evidence.title: Quarkonium production in heavy-ion collisions (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews ongoing uncertainties in cold nuclear matter effects and baseline references that complicate the interpretation of quarkonium suppression as a unique QGP signature.
status_evidence.claim: Baseline and cold nuclear matter uncertainties remain significant in interpreting quarkonium data.

status_evidence.title: Electromagnetic probes in heavy-ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses outstanding uncertainties in direct photon and dilepton measurements and their interpretation in terms of thermal QGP radiation versus hadronic sources.
status_evidence.claim: Interpretation of electromagnetic-probe data still subject to baseline and modeling uncertainties.
